transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Since my husband passed, it feels like everything inside me just shut down, and I can’t make myself do the things I used to care about. I just don't have it in me to do much of anything anymore.

Did these feelings of being 'shut down' and losing interest begin immediately following your husband's passing, or have you experienced similar periods of low mood and lack of motivation at other times in your life?

It didn't start right away, but crept in slowly over the first year after he passed. I've never felt anything like this before in my life, because I used to be so active with my church, mentoring, and my quilting circle. Before he died, I was always busy and involved.
Since your husband passed, have you experienced any persistent feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts that life is not worth living, even on your better days?

No, I don't really feel worthless or guilty, and I haven't thought about ending my life. It's just that I feel completely empty and shut down inside. I just can't find the energy or care to do anything anymore.
Beyond the lack of energy and interest, have you noticed other changes, such as significant shifts in your appetite, sleep patterns, or difficulty concentrating on simple tasks?
I haven't really noticed or thought much about changes in my sleep patterns. As for food, I just barely manage to eat simple meals without really thinking about my appetite.

Do you find that your current low mood and lack of motivation are specifically tied to thoughts and memories of your husband, or do you feel this sense of emptiness even when you are focused on other aspects of your life?

Although it started after he died, this emptiness isn't just about grieving him anymore. It feels like a switch has been turned off inside me generally, and I can't find the energy or interest for anything, even my quilting or choir.
Has this persistent feeling of being 'shut down' and the loss of interest in all your usual activities lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks or longer?

Yes, it's like this almost every single day, all day long. It's been much longer than just two weeks—it has actually been going on constantly for a little over two years now. I just can't seem to shake it.

Looking back at your life before your husband passed, can you recall any other distinct periods lasting two weeks or more where you felt this same persistent emptiness, lack of energy, or loss of interest in your activities?

No, I don't recall ever feeling this way before my husband passed away. Before his death, I was always very active and heavily involved in my church and my community. This numb, shut-down feeling is completely new to me.

Since this started two years ago, have there been any periods of a few months where you felt significantly better or back to your usual self, or has this low mood been present consistently the entire time?
No, there haven't been any times where I felt better or like my old self again. It has been this same heavy, shut-down feeling consistently for a little over two years now, without any break at all.
Since this started two years ago, has your mood been consistently low every single day, or have you had periods of a few weeks or months where you felt like your mood improved significantly?
No, it hasn't improved at all. It has been this exact same numb, shut-down feeling every single day for the last two years. I haven't had any periods where I felt better or like my old self again.

During these past two years, have you ever experienced any periods where you felt so slowed down that you were barely able to move or speak, or conversely, have you ever felt completely detached from reality or experienced things that others could not see or hear?

Yes, lately I get stuck standing in the hallway or kitchen for long stretches without moving or answering, or I find myself pacing and mumbling prayers. I've also been really scared because for the past few months, I regularly hear my late husband's voice talking to me from the garden or empty rooms. These things have been happening on top of that heavy, shut-down feeling I've had for the last two years.

To clarify, have you ever experienced a similar episode of feeling this 'shut down' accompanied by these same experiences of hearing voices or being unable to move before this current two-year period began?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. Before my husband passed away, I was very active in my church and community, and I never heard voices or felt "shut down" like this. All of this is completely new to me and only started after he died.

I have sufficient information to conclude the assessment.

As this is the patient's first such episode and there is no history of prior depressive episodes, F32.3 (Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe with psychotic symptoms) is the correct diagnosis rather than recurrent depression (F33.3).
